intention: A green seal names at least one tooth.
why: Law 8/9: a seal is green because teeth turned green; a green seal that names none asserts a color it cannot show, and a peer composes on it without re-checking — that is the one loss the proof-then-trust architecture cannot absorb. 31 of 224 green seals today are that.
how: (1) tester: in run_proof, after _teeth(stdout), a returncode of 0 with teeth_green == [] lands RED (detail 'zero teeth printed'), the same way a timeout lands red — the notary never says green over a proof that measured nothing it could name; one falsifier clause on the tester charter. (2) build_inspector: a deterministic RECORD sieve over each component's standing validations — a green verdict whose evidence lacks teeth_green or has it empty is a finding in the _finding shape (expected 'at least one tooth', actual N); it moves to postprocess when the shake ticket hands postprocess the stamps. (3) the corpus: reseal the 31, fix each red in the proof itself (a main() that runs every tooth and prints the names; 8 proofs have no __main__ at all, one imports pytest), never by exempting; measurement 31/209 -> 0. Proofs on both, sealed netns, hollow-read.
falsifier: DONE when (1) cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ has a tooth: TesterDevice().run_proof under a temp root on a fixture proof that exits 0 and prints no tooth name records verdict red with evidence.stderr_tail or a detail naming 'zero teeth printed', and on a fixture that prints one green tooth records green — sealed under netns; (2) cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/ has a tooth: the sieve over a fixture component whose validations hold a green record with teeth_green [] (and one with the key absent) returns one finding each in the _finding shape (about, expected, actual, compare), and over a green record naming a tooth returns none; the live assembly lists the sieve by name and phase_of derives it record; (3) the corpus census (green seals whose evidence names no tooth) reads 0 of N over cairn/**/validations, today 31 of 224, with every one of the 31 resealed green through the tester after its proof was given a runner that prints the tooth names, and no exemption list, allowlist, or skip anywhere in the tester or the sieve. RED if any green seal in the corpus names no tooth after the build, or if the tester can be made to say green over an empty teeth list by any argument. WRONG INTENT if a class of proof exists that legitimately cannot name a tooth (Akien's call, opened as a question) — the fix would still be a name, never an exemption.
traces_to: Law 8 (a hollow green is worse than a red: a green seal that names no teeth is a green nothing measured, and a peer leans on it) and Law 9 (green is earned; a seal is green because teeth turned green, and a seal with none listed asserts a color it cannot show); Law 3 (an unmeasured claim is a hypothesis — a green with no teeth is exactly an unmeasured green). Telos: the corpus's color is trustworthy enough to compose without re-checking.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Considered making the proof_coverage sieve at PROVEME (feeb4c786b14) demand a non-empty teeth list instead of touching the tester. It only fires at a crossing, so 31 standing seals would stay green forever; the notary is the one place every seal passes, and the inspector sieve is the one place every STANDING seal is read. Both are needed; this is the smaller shape that covers the corpus, not just new crossings.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That every honest proof prints its teeth through the one convention cairn.tools.proof_coverage.teeth_printed reads. A proof using a different marker would red under this rule and be 'fixed' by adopting the convention — that is the intended pressure, but it assumes the convention is the one mouth. Also assumes the tester's own timeout path (teeth_green == [], already red) and this path never disagree — they agree by construction since both land RED.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: Consulted the congruency lab: the tester charter's falsifier (9 clauses) says the notary must not lie but has no clause about a green that names nothing; feeb4c786b14 (coverage declared) reads teeth_green to judge a PROVEME crossing; hollow.py:524 reads teeth_green to compare; c5b6b128a376 reds UNRAN teeth at PROVEME. None reds an EMPTY teeth list on a standing green seal — measured 31 of 209 today, so the gap is real, not narrated. The finding shape he asked about (sieve name, expected, actual, pass/fail) already exists at build_inspector/inspector.py:94 _finding — no new shape.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: Law 7 says a record of truth never collapses an error; the change makes the tester REFUSE a green rather than collapse anything, so no collision. Possible chafe with 'a deterministic red is fixed or carries a decision': turning 31 greens red at once is 31 deterministic reds, and D2 says each is fixed in the proof — none carries a decision, none is plastered. Distinction to record: this reds the SEAL (the notary's claim), not the proof's exit code; the proof still exits 0, the tester just declines to call that green.
